_source: FC 27 closed beta, photographed 2026-08-12/13, build CL 9151217. Inputs read off the game's own Skill Moves screen — see ~/Desktop/fc26-controls-data/raw/fc27-beta-capture.md. Provisional until retail.
_note: Flair Nutmegs and Drag To Chop are NOT new to FC 27 — they existed and were missing from the web sources. They belong in the hub as corrections, not as their own pages.

moves.name: Giant Fake Shot
moves.what: A fake shot with a much larger body swing than the standard one — the full wind-up, then nothing.
moves.when: Standing still with a defender closing. The exaggerated motion sells harder than the normal fake shot, which is why it is a one-star move that still works against people who have seen a thousand fake shots.
moves.who: Everyone. One star means every build in the game can do it from level one, which makes it the single best value move on this list.
moves.note: It only fires from a standstill. Coming out of a sprint you get the ordinary fake shot.

moves.name: Stop And Go
moves.what: Kill the ball dead, then push off again in the same motion.
moves.when: Running at a retreating defender. The stop buys the half-yard their momentum costs them; the go takes it.
moves.who: Anything with Agility and Acceleration to punish the gap — but at two stars, most builds qualify.

moves.name: Drag To Drag
moves.ps: Hold L2 + ▢ or ◯ then hold ✕ or R ↓
moves.what: Two drags chained — the ball goes back under your body twice without a touch forward.
moves.when: Facing your own goal with pressure behind you. It is a possession move, not a beating move.
moves.who: Deep midfielders who receive with their back to play. A Maestro or Recycler uses this more than any winger will.

moves.name: Foot To Foot
moves.what: The ball is rolled from one foot to the other in a single quick transfer.
moves.when: Tight spaces where a full skill move would take too long. It shifts the ball a boot's width and changes which side you can strike from.
moves.who: Anyone with a decent weak foot — the whole point is finishing on the other side.

moves.name: Lateral Heel To Heel
moves.what: A heel-to-heel played sideways instead of forward and back.
moves.when: Running along a defensive line rather than at it. It moves you laterally without losing the ball forward, which is the standard heel-to-heel's weakness.

moves.name: Drag Turn
moves.what: Drag the ball back and turn out of it in one motion, exiting either side.
moves.when: Receiving under pressure. The drag creates the space, the turn decides where you go — and because the exit is a separate input, the defender cannot read it from the first movement.
moves.who: Any midfielder who receives facing their own goal.

moves.name: Standing Scoop Turn
moves.what: Scoop the ball up and turn under it from a standing start.
moves.when: Cornered on the touchline with no forward option. It buys a full rotation in almost no space.
moves.who: Technical forwards who get isolated wide.
moves.note: No shoulder button at all, which makes it unusually easy to fire by accident when you meant a fake shot.

moves.name: Flair Roulette
moves.what: The roulette, with the flair animation and a slightly wider turning arc.
moves.when: The same situations as the normal roulette — running into contact — but the wider arc clears a second defender the standard one does not.
moves.who: Players with the flair trait; the animation is slower, so it needs the space the extra arc buys.

moves.name: Four Touch Skill
moves.what: Four quick touches in sequence, moving the ball a short distance under close control.
moves.when: Beating a jockeying defender who is not committing. Four touches gives four chances for them to step, and the move ends with you still on the ball either way.
moves.who: Dribblers with high Ball Control — the touches are tight enough that a low rating loses it.

moves.name: Skilled Bridge
moves.what: Knock the ball through the defender's legs and run the other side of them.
moves.when: A defender square on with their feet apart — usually one who has just planted to jockey.
moves.who: Pace builds. The move puts the ball past them but you still have to win the footrace to it.

moves.name: First Time Spin
moves.what: Spin away from your marker on the first touch, before the ball has settled.
moves.when: Receiving a pass with a defender tight behind you. It is the only move on this list that happens *during* the first touch rather than after it.
moves.who: Five-star strikers who play with their back to goal.
moves.note: Two shoulder buttons and nothing else — the simplest input of any five-star move in the game.

moves.name: Alternate Elastico Chop
moves.ps: Hold L2 + R1 + flick R ↓ then ← or →
moves.what: An elastico that finishes with a chop instead of the usual push-out.
moves.when: When the defender has learned to read your elastico. The first half is identical; the finish is not.
moves.who: Five-star skillers who already use the elastico enough for opponents to anticipate it.

moves.name: Running Fake Drag
moves.what: A fake shot that becomes a drag, performed at full speed.
moves.when: Running at a defender who respects your shot. The fake stops them; the drag goes past them.
moves.who: Forwards with a shot worth respecting — the move only works if the fake is credible.
moves.note: The standing version of this is Giant Fake Shot at one star. This is the sprinting variant and costs four more stars.
